answer.rationale: With the contract expiring in 14 days and the line running at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, any delivery disruption is high-cost right now. Memory_c2 shows the low-cost vendor missed SLA in 3 of 4 quarters despite cost savings, making a full primary-vendor switch too risky under current no-slack conditions. Memory_c4 shows renegotiation at renewal previously recovered real margin (price and terms) without changing the incumbent relationship or introducing migration risk, which directly serves the finance mandate while protecting delivery continuity. Memory_c1 supports that incumbent continuity avoids integration/migration risk. I verify c4 and c2 specifically because they carry the most consequential and risk-relevant claims (savings mechanism and SLA failure rate) that this decision hinges on. Negotiating terms is the single action this cycle that addresses the cost mandate without gambling on an unproven or risky supply change; switching vendors or adding a second source are deferred to next cycle pending more capacity to manage transition risk.
